title: Azure AI Search: enforce Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels at indexing and query time
summary: Hold: the briefing presents an outage-specific, unlabelled-only fallback as the normal outcome of omitting the user token. It also overlooks documented native access controls outside sensitivity labels and incorrectly excludes preview SDKs from the available configuration methods.

claims.claim: Query-time label enforcement is documented as Public Preview, not general availability.

claims.claim: Query-time enforcement evaluates labels against the user's Microsoft Entra ID token and Purview label policies.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Ordinary label-enforced queries exclude labelled documents the requesting user is not authorised to retrieve.
claims.quote: If the user isn't authorized for a document's sensitivity label with EXTRACT permissions, that document is excluded from the query results.

claims.claim: Supported sources include Azure Blob Storage, ADLS Gen2, SharePoint document-library files and Microsoft OneLake.
claims.quote:
This functionality is available for the following data sources:
- Azure Blob Storage
- Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2
- SharePoint in Microsoft 365
- Microsoft OneLake

claims.claim: Sensitivity-label ingestion does not support SharePoint list items or site pages.
claims.quote: Sensitivity-label ingestion doesn't support SharePoint list items or site pages.

claims.claim: Source file types must be supported by both Purview sensitivity labels and Search indexers.
claims.quote: Use source documents with file types that are both supported by Purview sensitivity labels and supported by Foundry IQ indexers.

claims.claim: The Azure portal does not support this feature.
claims.quote: The Azure portal doesn't support this feature.

claims.claim: Autocomplete and Suggest are unsupported on Purview-enabled indexes.
claims.quote: Autocomplete and Suggest APIs aren't supported for Purview-enabled indexes, as they can't yet enforce label-based access control.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Guest accounts and cross-tenant queries are unsupported; the service and querying user must share a tenant.
claims.quote:

Guest accounts and cross-tenant queries aren't supported.

claims.claim: Labelled documents are not processed when the skillset or indexer uses a Custom Web API skill, knowledge store, enrichment cache or debug sessions.
claims.quote:
If you use any of these features in a skillset or indexer, documents with sensitivity labels aren't processed.
- Custom Web API skill
- Knowledge store
- Indexer enrichment cache
- Debug sessions

claims.claim: No admin UI is documented for setting an index's purviewEnabled property.
claims.quote: Searched: Azure AI Search Purview sensitivity labels purviewEnabled indexerPermissionOptions Azure portal configure. Read the indexer setup and document-level access overview; setup states the Azure portal does not support the feature.

claims.claim: PUT {endpoint}/indexes('{indexName}')?api-version=2026-11-01-preview supports the purviewEnabled request property.

PUT {endpoint}/indexes('{indexName}')?api-version=2026-11-01-preview
purviewEnabled | boolean | A value indicating whether Purview is enabled for the index.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: purviewEnabled must be true at index creation and cannot subsequently be changed.
claims.quote: The purviewEnabled property must be set to true when the index is created. This setting is permanent and can't be modified later.

claims.claim: No admin UI is documented for enabling sensitivityLabel extraction in a data source.
claims.quote: Searched: Azure AI Search Purview sensitivity labels purviewEnabled indexerPermissionOptions Azure portal configure. Read indexer setup steps 4-5 and the access overview; extraction uses API configuration and the Azure portal is unsupported.

claims.claim: PUT {endpoint}/datasources('{dataSourceName}')?api-version=2026-11-01-preview sets indexerPermissionOptions for sensitivity-label extraction.

PUT {endpoint}/datasources('{dataSourceName}')?api-version=2026-11-01-preview

claims.claim: Adding sensitivityLabel to indexerPermissionOptions should preserve any options already enabled.
claims.quote: Add sensitivityLabel to indexerPermissionOptions in your configured data source. If other permission options are already enabled, retain them and append this option rather than replacing the array.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Audit > Search reaches audit search.
claims.quote:
Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal.
Select the Audit solution card.
On the Search page, configure the following search criteria as applicable:

claims.claim: Search-UnifiedAuditLog searches the unified audit log.

claims.quote: You must be assigned the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs roles in the Microsoft Purview portal to search the audit log. To access audit cmdlets, you must be assigned the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs roles in the Exchange admin center.

claims.quote:
To investigate elevated read activity:

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Source label changes are not enforced from the index until a successful indexer run incorporates them.
claims.quote: The index doesn't reflect label changes on source documents until the next successful indexer run.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Why it matters; Governance guidance
claims.claim: An existing index without purviewEnabled true must be replaced with a Purview-enabled index and the pipeline retargeted.
claims.quote: If your existing index doesn't have purviewEnabled: true, create a new Purview-enabled index and retarget your indexer and any projection selectors to it. You can't enable this property on an existing index.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Elevated read bypasses the requesting user's per-document label permissions.
claims.quote: Foundry IQ skips the per-document label-based access check and returns matching documents, regardless of the requesting user's EXTRACT permissions on each label.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Elevated read emits one Purview audit entry for each document returned.
claims.quote: For each document in the response, Foundry IQ emits one entry to the Microsoft Purview audit log on behalf of the requesting tenant. A single search request that returns N documents produces N audit entries.

claims.claim: Elevated read requires Search Index Data Contributor on the service or index scope.
claims.quote: The calling developer user must hold the Search Index Data Contributor role on the Foundry IQ service or index scope. Search Index Data Reader isn't sufficient.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope: Prerequisites
claims.claim: Purview-enabled indexes require RBAC rather than API keys for document operations.
claims.quote: Purview-enabled indexes require RBAC authentication for document operations, including indexing content and querying. This configuration doesn't permit API-key document operations on Purview-enabled indexes.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Omitting the user-identity header normally succeeds with unlabelled-only results when the application has Search Index Data Reader.
claims.quote:
400 Bad Request
Microsoft Purview rejected the request because the x-ms-query-source-authorization header is absent, malformed, or the tenant isn't onboarded to Microsoft Purview Information Protection.
claims.fix: Replace both unqualified statements with: 'When Foundry IQ cannot reach Microsoft Purview, a non-elevated call without x-ms-query-source-authorization from an application with at least Search Index Data Reader succeeds with unlabelled-only results. Microsoft documents this degraded path only for non-user-facing workflows, not end-user search.' The same article documents a missing header among possible 400 errors; do not promise normal success without it.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Why it matters
claims.claim: Standard label-enforced requests fail with a 5xx error when Purview cannot be reached rather than returning unfiltered results.
claims.quote: Standard label-enforced requests (with x-ms-query-source-authorization): The request fails with 5xx. Foundry IQ doesn't return partial or unfiltered results when it can't evaluate label policies.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Enabling extraction on a previously processed pipeline does not make unchanged files eligible for a normal incremental run; the documented backfill resets and runs the indexer.
claims.quote: Enabling extraction, adding metadata fields, or retargeting the pipeline doesn't make unchanged files eligible for a normal incremental run. To reprocess those files, reset the indexer, then run it.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: A reset clears change tracking and its subsequent run reprocesses all source documents.
claims.quote: Reset clears change tracking and the subsequent run reprocesses all source documents; account for that workload.

claims.claim: Eligible paid Serverless services incur Compute Unit usage for indexer execution.
claims.quote: Eligible paid Serverless services incur Compute Unit usage for indexer execution, in addition to applicable index operations and storage.

claims.claim: Get Indexer Status is the documented way to confirm completion and inspect ingestion errors.
claims.quote: Use Get Indexer Status to confirm the execution completed successfully and inspect document errors and warnings. An accepted run request isn't proof of completed ingestion.

claims.claim: Running or scheduling the indexer refreshes detected source label changes.
claims.quote: For later incremental refresh, run or schedule the indexer to process detected source changes; don't reset it for every label refresh.

claims.where: Scope: Prerequisites; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Setup requires configuring Purview sensitivity-label policies and applying labels to documents before indexing.
claims.quote: Configure Microsoft Purview sensitivity label policies and apply them to documents before indexing.

claims.claim: The index stores a copy of document content.
claims.quote: When Foundry IQ indexes document content with sensitivity labels from sources like SharePoint, Azure Blob, and others, it stores both the content and the label metadata.

claims.where: Why it matters: Without label-aware indexing
claims.claim: Without label-aware indexing, access rules for indexed content are whatever the application builds.
claims.quote: SharePoint ACL ingestion and query-time permission filtering, ADLS Gen2 ACL/RBAC, and standard Blob container RBAC are generally available with the 2026-10-01 data plane REST API. Push ACL ingestion is also generally available.
claims.fix: Remove 'whose access rules are whatever the application builds'. The remaining sentence about an index being a second copy of the content can stay; do not imply that sensitivity labels are the only native document-access mechanism.

claims.where: Governance controls: The configuration is documented through REST and PowerShell only
claims.claim: REST and PowerShell are the only documented configuration methods.
claims.quote: Use REST API version 2026-11-01-preview or an equivalent preview SDK package.
claims.fix: Replace the sentence with: 'The index and data-source configuration uses REST or an equivalent preview SDK, while the documented role grants use PowerShell; the Azure portal does not support the feature.' In Open questions, replace 'REST and PowerShell only' with 'API, SDK and PowerShell based'.

claims.claim: The indexer article says READ while the query article says EXTRACT for retrieval rights.
claims.quote: Only users authorized to access content with READ usage right under a given label can retrieve corresponding documents in search results.

claims.claim: Usage rights are configured on sensitivity labels in Purview, not by the listed Search index and identity operations.
claims.quote: Usage rights are selected when you configure sensitivity labels or rights management templates for encryption. For example, you can select roles that configure a logical grouping of usage rights, or configure the individual rights separately.
claims.fix: Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/rights-management-usage-rights for the sentence about configuring label usage rights and add it to sources.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The roadmap describes built-in SharePoint, OneLake, Blob and ADLS Gen2 indexers supporting authorised-document retrieval for agentic RAG.
claims.quote: Azure AI Search now ingests Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels and enforces corresponding protection policies through built-in indexers (SharePoint, OneLake, Azure Blob, ADLS Gen2). This enables secure, policy-aligned search over enterprise data, enabling agentic RAG scenarios

claims.claim: The governance checklist asks readers to configure or check controls that have no matching table row.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'Decide which Purview labels must restrict content'; 'Reset and run the indexer'; 'Schedule the indexer'; 'Verify that agents pass the user token'. Table rows cover only index enforcement, extraction, managed-identity roles and audit review.
claims.fix: Limit the checklist to the controls already represented in the table: its label configuration, indexer reset/run/status, scheduling and query-token checks have no matching rows. Remove those unmatched checklist instructions; this correction does not require adding control rows.
